intended_object: For a profinite group G and a prime p, the inverse system U ↦ Syl_p(G/U), indexed by the open normal subgroups U of G. When U ≤ V, the transition map sends a Sylow p-subgroup of G/U to its image in G/V. Its inverse limit (its sections) is the set of compatible families of Sylow subgroups used in Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (1.6.9). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the way `CompatibleSylowFamily` uses it.
explanation:
The definition applies the generic `CompatibleSylow.system` to Mathlib's `ProfiniteGrp.toFiniteQuotientFunctor`. That functor sends U to G ⧸ U, and its maps U ⟶ V (meaning U ≤ V) are the quotient maps `QuotientGroup.map U V id`. These maps are surjective, which `quotientSylowTransition_surjective` proves.

`system` sends each object i to `Sylow p (F.obj i)`. On morphisms it uses `Sylow.mapSurjective`, which takes the image subgroup; under a surjective homomorphism of finite groups, the image of a Sylow p-subgroup is again a Sylow p-subgroup. The functor laws are proved correctly.

So the functor is exactly U ↦ Syl_p(G/U) with image maps, and its sections are precisely the compatible families of Sylow subgroups. There are no degenerate-case problems: Sylow subgroups exist for every prime and every finite group, possibly as the trivial subgroup.

On generality: the general construction for any surjective diagram of finite groups is already available as `CompatibleSylow.system`. This declaration is just its specialization to the canonical diagram of a profinite group, which is the object itself, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no corresponding definition.
